proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: each f in A has a unique finite Laurent expansion a-sharp(f) = sum f_n x^n, giving the coefficient maps f -> f_n; evaluating at x = 1 gives f = sum f_n (unit axiom of the action); the associativity axiom of the action yields the identity sum (f_n)_m x^m x^n = sum f_n x^n x^n, whence (f_n)_m = 0 for m not n and (f_n)_n = f_n; setting A_n = {f : f_n = f} gives A = sum A_n, and the sum is direct because the coefficient maps are well defined (source lines 2563-2587)

core_obligations: Coefficient decomposition (proof lines 2564-2572): the Laurent expansion gives well-defined finite coefficient maps f -> f_n; the unit axiom (evaluation at x = 1) gives f = sum f_n.
Grading identities (proof lines 2572-2582): the associativity axiom a(a(f)) = a(f) expanded coefficientwise gives (f_n)_m = 0 for m != n and (f_n)_n = f_n.
Directness (proof lines 2582-2587): A = sum A_n by the previous step; the sum is direct since the coefficient maps are well defined, so f = 0 implies all f_n = 0.
proof_roadmap: Extract the coefficient maps from the Laurent expansion (proof lines 2564-2572).
Use the unit and associativity axioms to get the grading identities (proof lines 2572-2582).
Conclude A is the direct sum of its graded pieces (proof lines 2582-2587).
